steps.title: Obtain raw FASTQ data
steps.instruction: Collect raw sequencing reads in FASTQ format.

steps.title: Filter reads with SOAPnuke
steps.instruction: Run SOAPnuke v1.5.6 on the FASTQ files using parameters "-l 5 -q 0.5 -n 0.1 -Q 2 --seqType 0" to filter low‑quality sequences.

steps.title: Estimate genome size via k‑mer
steps.instruction: Perform 17‑mer analysis on ~27.7 Gb of filtered reads; calculate genome size (~650 Mb) using G = N*(L‑17+1)/K_depth, where N and L are total read count and read length, and K_depth is the peak k‑mer depth.

steps.title: Assemble genome with SOAPdenovo2
steps.instruction: Execute SOAPdenovo2 v2.04.4 on the filtered reads using all insert‑size libraries. Run the modules sequentially: pregraph with -K 57 -p 10, contig with -g, map with -p 10 -k 39, and scaff with -p 10.

steps.title: Close gaps with krskgf and Gapcloser
steps.instruction: Apply krskgf v1.19 followed by Gapcloser v1.10 to the SOAPdenovo2 assembly to close remaining gaps.

steps.title: Build repeat library with RepeatModeler
steps.instruction: Run RepeatModeler on the assembled genome to generate a de‑novo repeat library.

steps.title: Mask repeats with RepeatMasker
steps.instruction: Run RepeatMasker v3.3.0 using the library from step 6 as database, with parameters "-nolow -no_is -norna -parallel 1" to mask identified repeats.

steps.title: Identify repeats with TRF and RepeatProteinMask
steps.instruction: Run TRF v4.09, RepeatMasker and RepeatProteinMask v3.3.0 against Repbase v17.01; for RepeatProteinMask use parameters "-noLowSimple -pvalue 0.0001" to detect DNA‑ and protein‑level repeats.

steps.title: Mask repetitive regions with Ns
steps.instruction: Replace the repeat regions identified in steps 6‑8 with Ns in the genome sequence before gene prediction.

steps.title: Predict genes with Augustus
steps.instruction: Run Augustus v2.5.5 on the repeat‑masked genome using parameters "--species=Lateolabrax_maculatus --uniqueGeneId=true --noInFrameStop=true --gff3=on --strand=both".

steps.title: Predict genes with Genscan
steps.instruction: Run Genscan v2.1 on the same repeat‑masked genome with default parameters.

steps.title: Homology‑based prediction with BLAT and GeneWise
steps.instruction: Download teleost protein sequences (Danio rerio, D. labrax, Gasterosteus aculeatus, Lates calcarifer, Oreochromis niloticus, Oryzias latipes, Tetraodon nigroviridis, Takifugu rubripes; NCBI IDs provided). Align them to the masked genome using BLAT, then run GeneWise v2.2.0 on the alignments with parameters "--max divergence rate 0.3 --extend length for both sides of regions 2000" to predict genes.

steps.title: Transcriptome‑based prediction with Trinity data
steps.instruction: Download spotted sea bass transcriptome assembled by Trinity v2013.11 from NCBI, map the transcripts to the genome with BLAT, and collapse redundant gene models using default parameters.

steps.title: Combine predictions with GLEAN
steps.instruction: Integrate gene models from Augustus, Genscan, GeneWise, and transcriptome‑based predictions using GLEAN; filter results with overlap cutoff 0.8 and require at least one homolog support.

steps.title: Add manually curated genes
steps.instruction: Incorporate genes supported by transcriptome data and D. labrax prediction after manual curation into the GLEAN consensus set.

steps.title: Functional annotation of final gene set
steps.instruction: Map the final protein sequences to SwissProt, TrEMBL and KEGG using BLASTP; run InterProScan v4.7 with seven models (Profilescan, blastprodom, HmmSmart, HmmPanther, HmmPfam, FPrintScan, Pattern‑Scan) to assign motifs and domains.
